findings.evidence: `id="s3-step3" style="order:3"` appears first in the markup, before `id="s3-step2" style="order:2"` and `id="s3-step1" style="order:1"`
findings.fix: Put the elements in the DOM in the same order they should be read/navigated, rather than reordering visually with CSS.
findings.violation: CSS `order` makes the visible sequence "Choose a plan → Enter payment details → Confirm your order," but the DOM/reading order is the reverse, so screen readers and sequential keyboard navigation encounter the steps backwards.

findings.evidence: `read the accessibility improvements list` inside "For the full list of upcoming adjustments..."
findings.fix: Change the link text to accurately describe the destination (e.g., "read the full list of upcoming schedule changes") and verify the href points to the correct page.
findings.violation: The link text says "accessibility improvements list," but it sits in the "Schedule changes" section discussing schedule adjustments and points to "/fares/history" - the text matches neither the surrounding content nor the destination.

findings.fix: Add a text indicator such as "(required)" or an asterisk with an accessible label, and set `required`/`aria-required="true"` on the input.
findings.violation: Red text is the only signal that this field differs from the others (presumably required), which conveys no information to colorblind users or screen reader users.

findings.evidence: `` ... `Error.`
findings.fix: Only apply `aria-invalid="true"` after a failed validation, add `aria-describedby="s3-form-promo-error"` to the input, and replace "Error." with a specific message like "Promo code is invalid."
findings.location: s3-form promo input and error span
findings.violation: The field is marked invalid statically with no prior user input or validation trigger, and it lacks `aria-describedby` linking it to the error span, so screen reader users get no explanation tied to the field.

findings.evidence: `<select id="topic">`, `<input id="email" type="email" autocomplete="email">`, `<input id="phone" type="tel" autocomplete="tel">`, `<input id="promo" type="text" aria-invalid="true">`
findings.violation: None of the form controls has a `name` attribute, so their values won't be submitted with the form.
